text:
alex: Heads up — Support flagged a high-severity customer report: p95/p99 for /v1/generate jumped ~2x after last night's runtime rollforward (runtime v3.2.3 -> v3.2.4). Customer traffic route: eu-west-1, model: redwood-ggml-13b, typical seq len ~512.

maria: I see the alert in the dashboard. Canary looked fine but global rollout completed at 23:40 UTC. Can you paste the metric graphs? p95 and p99 please.

sre-bot: deploy: rollout completed for runtime/v3.2.4 by @maria at 2026-03-16T23:40:12Z. Canary window passed (15m).

alex: Uploaded screenshots to the ticket but summary: p95 180ms -> 360ms, p99 420ms -> 950ms on generator path. No obvious error count spike, success rate still >99.9%. Latency spike correlated with increased qlength on request-queue metric.

jon: Did we change the kernel selector or batching defaults in this release? I remember a kernel fallback tweak was merged.

maria: Yes — change set includes: adaptive-kernel-selector (fallback order change), queueing/backpressure tweak (max_inflight default lowered from 128 -> 64), and small tweak to cold-prefix cache TTL.

sam: Lowering max_inflight can increase head-of-line wait if a hot path dominates. Could cause higher tail latencies for big requests. Do we have request size histogram?

alex: Customer mentioned some long prompts (800-1200 tokens) which would force slow-path chunking. I attached a minimal repro (anonymized):

```
POST /v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer <key>
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "model":"redwood-ggml-13b",
  "input":"<~800 token prompt...>",
  "max_tokens":512,
  "stream":false
}
```

jon: Good repro. Can we reproduce internally with a traffic mix of bursty large-seq requests? I can spin up a replay against canary and prod.

maria: Do not hit prod with replay without scheduling. Start a small load against a staging cluster that has v3.2.4. Also capture KV cache hit rates — note the cache TTL change.

sam: I started a short run on staging. Early notes: when concurrency is high and there are a handful of long-seq requests, queue length increases and we see p99 spike due to serialization in the model-worker queue. The kernel selector fallback path is slightly slower on these sequences.

support-bot: Customer escalation acknowledged. Support will create a call if needed. Alex, please share correlation window and customer contact.

alex: Escalation ticket #INC-2026-1147 created. Customer is available for a call 14:00 UTC. I added logs and request IDs.

maria: Immediate mitigation options: 1) rollback runtime v3.2.4 to v3.2.3 global, 2) apply traffic split (canary-style) divert 50% to v3.2.3 for eu-west-1, 3) bump max_inflight back to 128 remotely (hot-config) while we bisect. Thoughts?

jon: Prefer traffic split for minimal blast radius. Rollback if split doesn't help. We should also try toggling the kernel selector flag to force old order (hot-config) to test whether that is the culprit.

sam: I agree — try hot-config to set max_inflight=128 and kernel-selector=legacy in eu-west-1 for a test window, then monitor p95/p99 for 10m. I can apply and watch.

maria: I will prepare a short canary traffic-split and grant jon/sam access to the rollout UI. Also adding a one-line alert that p99 > 700ms for > 5m in eu-west-1 to catch regressions.

sre-bot: config-change: hot-config applied to cluster eu-west-1: max_inflight=128 by @sam at 2026-03-17T00:08:03Z.

sam: After hot-config change — preliminary: p95 dropped to ~210ms, p99 to ~480ms within 3 minutes. Queue length normalized. Looks promising.

alex: I notified the customer; they see improved response times in their environment too.

jon: Next: bisect the release to pinpoint offending commit. Candidate PRs: #4422 (adaptive-kernel-selector reorder), #4441 (backpressure default change), #4447 (cache TTL tweak). We should binary search by toggling each feature via hot-config and/or doing short A/B rollouts.

maria: Agreed. Sam, can you toggle kernel-selector back to legacy and see effect? Jon, can you run a binary split on the backpressure change next. We want to confirm which one moves the tail.

sam: Toggling kernel-selector=legacy now.

sre-bot: config-change: kernel-selector=legacy applied to eu-west-1 by @sam at 2026-03-17T00:17:41Z.

sam: After kernel-selector flip: no measurable change beyond the improvement we already got from max_inflight bump. Suggests backpressure change was the dominant factor.

jon: I'll run a short A/B where 25% traffic uses runtime with backpressure default=128 and 75% uses 64.

maria: Make sure to capture request-level tracing and include request ids for the customer repro. Also check kernel fallback counts — if not necessary we can revert that change but that looks orthogonal.

jon: A/B done — p99 on the 25% cohort is back to baseline, 75% cohort remains elevated. Bisect points to #4441 (backpressure default) as root cause.

sam: Proposal: revert #4441 and issue v3.2.5 that keeps other fixes but keeps max_inflight at previous default. Create a follow-up to revisit a safer rollout (gradual tuning and load testing with long-seq workload).

maria: Agreed. I'll coordinate the revert PR and patch release. Also adding a postmortem action: add long-seq workload to canary test harness and add a smoke test for concurrency vs large token requests.

alex: Support note for customer: we're rolling a patch now and will confirm after deploy. Thanks for the quick triage.

sre-bot: rollback-pr: opened #4501 to revert backpressure default change. patch-release/v3.2.5 scheduled.

support-bot: Customer informed. Will keep customer updated and schedule 14:00 UTC call as backup.

maria: Post-action: after v3.2.5 rollout, we need to track p95/p99 for 6 hours and then close the incident. Also add learning doc to eng-runtime/handbook about safe backpressure rollouts.

alex: Closing loop with customer once metrics stable. Great work team :thumbsup:
